anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of On Pascha exists (Toura 1941; Daly ACW 54 and Witte's German are copyrighted and were not copied). Sense checked against the locked Witte Greek (and, for 1.94, Victor of Capua's Latin as Witte prints it) and the wording of the cited scriptures.

bible_refs.note: Quoted: unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood, you have no life in yourselves.

choices.why: Opposed to αἰσθητόν, the sense-level feast.
Origen's verb for the raw/roast problem later.

pass_a_gloss: And that the pascha is intelligible and not this sensible, he himself says: Unless you eat my flesh and drink my blood, you have no life in yourselves. Must we then chew his fleshes according to sense and drink his blood? But if he says this intelligibly, then intelligible and not sensible is the pascha.
pass_b_english: [And] that the Passover [is intelligible] and not [this sensible one], he himself [says: "Unless] you eat my [flesh] and drink my blood, you have no life [in] yourselves." Must we then chew his flesh according to sense and drink his blood? But if he says this intelligibly, then the Passover too is intelligible and not sensible.
source_text: [Καὶ ] ὅ[τ]ι [νοητόν ἐστι] τὸ πάσχα [καὶ] οὐ τ[οῦτο τὸ αἰσθη]τόν, α[ὐτὸς] λέγ[ει· "Ἐὰν μ]ὴ φάγη[τ]έ μο[υ [τὴν σάρ]κα καὶ πί[η]τέ μο[υ τὸ] αἷμα, οὐκ ἔχετε ζωὴ[ν ἐν] ἑαυτοῖς". Ὀφείλομ[εν ἄρ]α κατὰ αἰσθητὸν τὰς [σ]άρκας αὐτοῦ τρώγειν καὶ τὸ αἷμα αὐτοῦ πίνειν; Εἰ δὲ τοῦτο νοητῶς λέγει, ἄρα νοητὸν καὶ οὐκ αἰσθητόν ἐστι τὸ πάσχα.
